question: In 1879, who observed cell division in salamander embryos, where cells divide at fixed intervals?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Walther Flemming.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flemming** observed cell division in salamander embryos, where cells divide at fixed intervals.
 
• He developed a way to stain chromosomes to observe them clearly.
 
• **The first person to observe mitosis in detail was a German biologis**t, **Walther Flemming** (1843–1905), who is the pioneer of mitosis research and also** the founder of cytogenetics (Paweletz 2001).**
 
• **Walther Flemming was** a pioneer of **cytogenetics**, a field of **science that analyses structures and processes in the cell nucleus under a microscope.**
 
• He was the first person to conduct a systematic study of chromosomes during division and called this **process mitosis.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**
